column2: 1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon mint, 1 teaspoon chilli flakes
Blanch the chard leaves in boiling water for 1 minute and remove the stalks.
Fry the onion and make a filling with rice, tomato paste, parsley and spices.
Roll up the leaves with the filling.
Arrange in a pot, add hot water and cover with a plate.
On the Black Sea coast, chard rolls are also made with mince.
Sour cabbage (Black Sea style)
1 kg pickled cabbage
Chop the pickled cabbage and rinse it if it’s too salty.
Fry the onion in butter and add the chilli flakes.
Add the pickled cabbage and rice, then 1 cup water.
Serve with cornbread.
Don’t add salt, as the pickled cabbage is salty.
Chicken güveç (clay-pot casserole)
8 shallots
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon thyme
Arrange the chicken and vegetables in the clay pot.
Thin the tomato paste with butter and 1 cup hot water and pour over.
Sprinkle with the spices and cover the pot.
Put in a cold oven and cook at 200 °C for 60 minutes.
A clay pot goes into a cold oven.
Sac kavurma (sautéed meat on a griddle)
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes, 1 teaspoon thyme
Heat the sac griddle or a wide cast-iron pan thoroughly.
Sear the meat over a high heat until it releases its juices and they evaporate.
Add the butter and chopped onion.
Add the peppers and tomatoes and toss for 5 more minutes.
Season with the spices and serve with lavash.
Cooking in small batches stops the meat from stewing.
Boiled lamb
1 kg lamb on the bone
1 dessert spoon salt, 5 black peppercorns
Put the meat in cold water, bring to the boil and skim off the foam.
Add the onion, peppercorns and celeriac and cook over a low heat for 1.5 hours.
Add the roughly chopped carrots and potatoes.
Cook 25 more minutes until the vegetables are tender, and add salt.
The cooking broth can be used in soups.
Liver wrapped in caul fat (ciğer sarma)
400 g lamb’s liver
1 lamb’s caul fat
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon cumin, 1 teaspoon black pepper
Dice the liver small and mix with finely chopped onion and spices.
Soften the caul fat in lukewarm water and cut into squares.
Wrap the filling in the caul fat and secure with a cocktail stick.
Cook on a grill or in a 200 °C oven for 20–25 minutes.
Serve with sumac onions.
Liver must be thoroughly cooked; it should not stay pink inside.
Steamed anchovies (hamsi buğulama)
Remove the heads of the anchovies, clean and wash them.
Arrange onion rings and peppers on the bottom of the pot.
Lay the anchovies side by side on top and cover with tomato and lemon slices.
Add olive oil and salt and steam, covered, over a low heat for 15 minutes.
No need to add water; the vegetables release liquid.
Grilled sea bass
2 whole sea bass (cleaned)
To serve: rocket and red onion (1 bunch, 1 onion)
Score the fish diagonally.
Rub with olive oil and salt.
Cook on a hot grill for 5–6 minutes on each side.
It’s cooked when the flesh comes away easily from the bones.
Serve with lemon and rocket salad.
Heating the grill thoroughly stops the fish sticking.
Octopus salad
1 kg octopus
Cook the octopus in its own juices in boiling water for 45 minutes, until a fork goes in easily.
When cool, slice the tentacles 1 cm thick.
Finely chop the onion, pepper and parsley.
Mix with olive oil, lemon and salt.
Chill in the fridge for 1 hour, then serve.
Frozen octopus tenderises more easily.
Tutmaç soup (noodle and lentil yogurt soup)
For the noodles: 1 cup flour, 1 egg, 1 teaspoon salt
1 dessert spoon dried mint, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes, 1 dessert spoon salt
Knead a firm dough with flour, egg and salt, roll out thinly and cut into small squares.
Boil the lentils in 6 cups water for 20 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook for 10 minutes.
Temper the yogurt and egg yolk and add; remove from the heat just before it boils.
Drizzle with butter flavoured with mint and chilli flakes.
An Anatolian soup known since Seljuk times.
Lebeniye soup (yogurt and chickpea)
1 dessert spoon dried mint, 1 dessert spoon salt
Cook the rice in 5 cups water for 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas.
Whisk the yogurt, egg and flour, temper and add.
Cook, stirring constantly, until it boils.
Often made in Hatay and Antep cuisine.
Mahluta (Hatay lentil soup)
1 dessert spoon cumin, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes, 1 dessert spoon salt
Add the washed lentils, rice and 6 cups hot water.
Cook for 30 minutes and blend.
Add the cumin and salt.
Serve with chilli butter and lemon.
Cumin is the distinctive flavour of mahluta.
Ayran aşı soup (cold yogurt soup)
Half a cup whole wheat (boiled)
Half a cup chickpeas (boiled)
3 cups yogurt
1 bunch spinach or chard
Whisk the yogurt, egg, flour and 4 cups water.
Add the wheat, chickpeas and chopped greens.
Cook for 10 minutes and add salt.
Serve hot, or cold in summer.
An Anatolian soup drunk cold in summer.
Hot or cold.
Paçanga börek (pastırma and kashar rolls)
4 sheets yufka
150 g pastırma
150 g kashar
1 cup oil for frying
Cut the yufka into triangles.
Finely chop the pastırma, kashar, tomato and pepper.
Put the filling on the yufka, roll up like sigara börek and seal the end with egg.
Fry in hot oil for 2 minutes on each side.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.
A hot meze from Istanbul’s meyhane (tavern) cuisine.
Çiğ börek (raw-mince fried turnovers)
Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 cup water, 1 dessert spoon salt
Filling: 300 g mince, 2 grated onions, 1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper
Knead the mince with the onion, salt and pepper and leave it raw.
Roll out the dough thinly, spread the filling thinly over half, fold over and press the edges.
